/di/

Number

  1. A Roman numeral representing five hundred one (501).

Preposition

  1. used to indicate possession, after the thing owned and before the owner; of; ’s
  2. from
  3. by, of, ’s
  4. than
  5. used in superlative forms; in, of
  6. about, on, concerning
  7. expresses composition; of, made of, in or more often omitted
  8. (followed by an infinitive) to or omitted
  9. used with the definite article in partitive constructions; some
  10. used in some expressions in a partitive-like function, often without article
  11. (idiomatic) used alongside spatial adverbs qua / qui or là / lì, also with preceding per

Noun f.

  1. The name of the Latin script letter D/d.; dee

Usage Note

  1. When followed by the definite article, di combines with the article to produce the following combined forms:
  2. The i can additionally optionally be elided before vowel sounds to form d'.

From Latin dē. Cognate with English to. For etymology 1, preposition sense 11, compare French delà, deçà and deci delà.

From Latin dē (the name of the letter D).

/doˈve.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to owe
  2. (auxiliary) to have to do something (must)

Noun m.

  1. duty

Interjection

  1. Dismisses gratitude by clarifying one acted for one's duty rather than for kindness.

Usage Note

  1. As an auxiliary, dovere takes avere or essere, depending on the verb that follows it.
  2. All conditional forms, like dovrei, are translated as should.

Inherited from Latin dēbēre (“to owe”). Cognate with Sicilian duviri.

/ˈfa.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to do
  2. (transitive) to make
    1. to create
    2. to bring about
    3. to behave or act [with da ‘as’]
    4. to constitute
    5. to numerically result in; to add up to
    6. to formulate in the mind
    7. to cause to be; to render
    8. (ditransitive) to compel
    9. (ditransitive) to force
  3. to provoke (a physical sensation)
  4. (transitive) to inflict (damage, pain, etc.) on
  5. (transitive) to cause or arouse (an emotion)
  6. (transitive) to draw up or enter into (a contract, agreement, etc.)
  7. (transitive) to emit from the body
  8. (transitive) to have (a baby)
  9. (transitive) to produce a lot of (fruit or flowers) (of a plant)
  10. (transitive) to have (a certain population) (of a state, country, etc.)
  11. (transitive, informal) to cost
    1. to sell [with a ‘for (a price)’]
  12. (transitive) to clean up
  13. (transitive) to address
  14. (transitive) to organize or celebrate (an event, party, etc.)
  15. (transitive) to stage (a play, movie, etc.)
    1. to produce or participate in (a play, movie, etc.) (of a director, actor, etc.)
    2. to interpret (a role, character, etc.); to act
    3. to be planned or scheduled (at a certain time) [with a or in] (of a movie, show, etc., chiefly in the form fanno)
  16. (transitive) to be subscribed to; to do regularly
    1. to attend (a school), to be in (a grade level)
    2. to practice (a hobby, sport, etc.)
  17. (transitive) to follow (a road, etc.)
  18. (transitive) to visit (a country, city, etc.)
  19. (transitive) to last (an amount of time)
    1. (transitive, informal) to turn (an age)
  20. (transitive, informal) to gift
  21. (transitive) to tell or indicate (the time)
  22. (transitive) to do until (a time, typically at night)
  23. (transitive) to caricature
  24. (transitive) to spend; to pass (of time)
  25. (transitive) to live or lead (a kind of life)
  26. (transitive) to pronounce, judge, or evaluate
  27. (transitive) (with che + subj.) to suppose or consider
  28. (transitive) to gather
    1. (transitive) to stock up on
  29. (transitive) to work as (a profession)
  30. (transitive) to elect or nominate
  31. (transitive, sports, card games) to score
  32. (transitive) to make appear
    1. to create impressions of
  33. (transitive) (with inf.) to let
  34. (transitive) (with [di + inf.] or [che + subj.]) to strive or endeavor
  35. (intransitive) to be suitable [with per ‘for’] [auxiliary avere]
  36. (intransitive) to play [with a] [auxiliary avere]
  37. (intransitive) to be spent or to have gone by; to mark [auxiliary avere] (of time)
  38. (intransitive, impersonal) to be (hot, cold, etc.) [auxiliary avere] (of the weather, climate, etc.)
  39. (intransitive, grammar) to have as an inflected form [auxiliary avere] (of a word)
  40. (intransitive) to go (to say something or make a sound) [auxiliary avere]
  41. (intransitive) to go (to be expressed or composed) [auxiliary avere]
  42. (intransitive) to be formed by a sequence [auxiliary avere]
  43. (intransitive, with come (“how”)) to be able to [with a (+ infinitive); or with per (+ infinitive)] [auxiliary avere]
  44. (intransitive, rare) to take root [auxiliary avere] (of a plant)
  45. (intransitive, rare) to suffice [auxiliary avere] (of a plant)

Noun m.

  1. manner, way

Usage Note

  1. fa' + mi = fammi
    1. ... + lo = fammelo
    2. ... + la = fammela
    3. ... + le = fammele
    4. ... + li = fammeli
    5. ... + ne = fammene
  2. fa' + ti = fatti
    1. ... + lo = fattelo
    2. ... + la = fattela
    3. ... + le = fattele
    4. ... + li = fatteli
    5. ... + ne = fattene
  3. fa' + gli = fagli and fa' + le = falle
    1. ... + lo = faglielo
    2. ... + la = fagliela
    3. ... + le = fagliele
    4. ... + li = faglieli
    5. ... + ne = fagliene
  4. fa' + ci = facci
    1. ... + lo = faccelo
    2. ... + la = faccela
    3. ... + le = faccele
    4. ... + li = facceli
    5. ... + ne = faccene
  5. fa' + lo = fallo
  6. fa' + la = falla
  7. fa' + le = falle
  8. fa' + li = falli
  9. fa' + ne = fanne

Inherited from Late Latin fāre.

/ˈfar.si/

Verb

  1. to become
  2. to make oneself
  3. to elaborate on in one's mind
  4. to form (a relationship, friendship, etc.) with
  5. to acquire or buy
    1. Synonyms: prendersi, comprarsi
  6. to eat or drink
  7. to smoke (a cigarette, pipe, etc.)
    1. Synonym: fumarsi
  8. to move oneself
  9. (with a) to look out (the window, etc.)
    1. Synonym: affacciarsi
  10. to let
    1. Synonym: lasciare
  11. to compel or force
  12. to become an expert
    1. Synonym: migliorarsi
  13. to exchange (between or among each other)
  14. (impersonal) to become (of time)
  15. to facilitate its usage; to be easy (to use) (of a tool, etc.)
    1. Synonym: lasciarsi
  16. (slang) to do (take drugs)
  17. (slang, vulgar) to make, have (sexually)
    1. Synonyms: chiavare, scopare, trombare, fottere

From fare (“to do, make”) +‎ -si (“oneself”).

/ˈtɛm.po/

Noun m.

  1. (uncountable) time
  2. time, age, period
  3. part (of a film, show, etc.)
  4. weather
    1. Synonym: clima — proscribed
  5. (music) time, tempo, rhythm, beat, pulse
  6. (grammar) tense

From Latin tempus (“time”), from Proto-Indo-European *tempos (“stretch”), from the root *temp- (“to stretch, string”).
